blocks.source: Cum mundus in caligine reatum jacet Et haeresisum fuligine Suffusis indoleret: Rerum supremus arbiter

When the world lies in the darkness of guilt

By the soot of heresies,
The supreme Ruler of all things

blocks.source: Deus, qui ad majorem Nominis tui gloriam, propagandam novo per B. Ignatium subsidium militantem Ecclesiam roborasti; concede, ut ejus auxilio, et imitatione certantes in terris, coronari cum ipso mereamur in caelis. Qui vivis et regnas, etc.
blocks.english: O God, who, for the spreading of the greater glory of Thy Name, didst strengthen the Church militant through blessed Ignatius with a new aid, grant that, striving on earth with his help and in imitation of him, we may deserve to be crowned with him in heaven. blocks.source: Sublimis inter aera Ignatius tenetur: Quando te ulgens sidera precando conatur Apostolos in judicium ab legat hinc vereptum: Cum caeteris exotiicum hic, excolit rosetum. Aufert suorum cordibus sodalium pavorem Cum Christus ipsis omnibus proponit et favorem.
blocks.english:
Ignatius is held aloft in the air;
[The printed “Quando te ulgens sidera precando conatur” is unresolved.]
[The printed “Apostolos in judicium ab legat hinc vereptum” is unresolved.]
With the others, here he cultivates [the printed “exotiicum” is unresolved] a rose garden.
He removes fear from the hearts of his companions,
When Christ sets before them all His favour.
blocks.editorialNote: Several middle lines are corrupt, including “te ulgens,” “ab legat,” “vereptum,” and “exotiicum.” Their meanings remain unresolved rather than importing a known biographical episode.

blocks.source: Jam vitis illicae sersperat Ignatio fatore, Orbemque ferme sersperat coelestium favore. Cum strenui mens militis post haec relicta castra Inepta nomen coelitis poli subivit astra. O Patriarcha, lumine dignare nos paterno! Opemque natis, lumine transmittente de superno.
blocks.english:
[The printed “Jam vitis illicae sersperat Ignatio fatore” is unresolved.]
And almost the whole world [the printed “sersperat” is unresolved] through the favour of the heavenly ones.
When the mind of the valiant soldier, having left this camp,
[The printed “Inepta nomen coelitis” is unresolved], rose to the stars of heaven.
O Patriarch, deign to look upon us with a father’s light!
And send help to thy children, with light shining from on high.
blocks.editorialNote: “illicae,” “sersperat,” “fatore,” and “Inepta nomen coelitis” are corrupt or uncertain. The readable prayer for paternal light and help is retained; the other clauses remain unresolved.

blocks.source: Haec vota supplex offero Ignatio praesenti, Et hunc honorem defero majora potenti. Exopto per te maximi nunc ponderis favorem, Tum Numinis, tum proximi terris in his amorem. Ut mens soluta corpore festaret ad superna, Et pace pleno pectore fruatur cive aeterna.
blocks.english:
A suppliant, I offer these vows to Ignatius present,
And render this honour to him who can do greater things.
Through thee I now desire a favour of the greatest weight:
Love both of God and of my neighbour here on earth;
That the mind, freed from the body, may hasten unto things above,
And with a breast full of peace may enjoy [the printed “cive aeterna” is uncertain].
blocks.editorialNote: “festaret” and “cive aeterna” are irregular. “May hasten” is provisional; the final object of enjoyment remains uncertain.

blocks.source: Oratio recitanda ante Imaginem S. Ignatii
blocks.english: Prayer to be recited before an image of Saint Ignatius

blocks.source: Salve Sancte Patriarcha Ignati, imitator Jesu Christi; templum Spiritus Sancti; serve amantissime SS. Trinitatis! Salve emulator Martyrum; imago Apostolorum, Vas electionis. Salve expugnator vitiorum, compendium virtutum, idea perfectionis. Salve norma patientiae; castitatis lilium, modestiae speculum. Salve obedientiae prodigium, charitatis ignis, pauperum refugium. Salve exemplar abstinentiae, humilitatis prototypon, afflictorum solatium. Auxiliare Magister ignorantium, dux poenitentium, reformator Christi; norum illumina mentem meam, dux infidelium Guberna cor meum, magne affectuum tuorum moderator. Impetra mihi veniam, felicissimae pacis conciliator. Excra in bono perseverantiam, firma Ecclesiae columna. Intercede pro me, meisque omnibus, tum consanguineis, tum amicis et benefactoribus; strenue clientium tuorum Protector. Sis mihi scutum in adversitatibus; defende me in tentationibus, et omnibus in vita malis, nec me deferas in hora mortis meae. Amen.
blocks.english: Hail, holy Patriarch Ignatius, imitator of Jesus Christ, temple of the Holy Ghost, most loving servant of the most Holy Trinity! Hail, emulator of the Martyrs, image of the Apostles, vessel of election. Hail, conqueror of vices, compendium of virtues, pattern of perfection. Hail, rule of patience, lily of chastity, mirror of modesty. Hail, marvel of obedience, fire of charity, refuge of the poor. Hail, example of abstinence, model of humility, comfort of the afflicted. Help us, teacher of the ignorant, leader of penitents, [the printed “reformator Christi; norum” is unresolved]; illumine my mind, leader of unbelievers; govern my heart, great moderator of thine affections. Obtain pardon for me, bringer of most blessed peace. Obtain perseverance in good, firm pillar of the Church. Intercede for me and all mine, both kinsfolk and friends and benefactors, vigorous protector of thy clients. Be my shield in adversity; defend me in temptations and from all evils in life, and forsake me not at the hour of my death. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “reformator Christi; norum” is unresolved. “Excra” is rendered provisionally as “obtain,” and “deferas” as “forsake.” The remainder of the printed prayer is preserved.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Ego Dominus vocavi te in justitia, et apprehendi manum tuam, et servavi te, et dedi te in foedus populi; in lucem gentium, ut aperies oculos caecorum, et educeres de conclusione vinctum, de domo carceris sedentem in tenebris.
blocks.english: I, the Lord, have called thee in justice, and taken thy hand, and preserved thee, and given thee for a covenant of the people, for a light of the nations, that thou mightest open the eyes of the blind, and bring forth the prisoner from confinement, and him that sits in darkness from the prison house.

blocks.source: ℣. Annunciate inter gentes gloriam ejus.
blocks.english: ℣. Declare His glory among the nations.

blocks.source: ℟. In omnibus populis mirabilia ejus.
blocks.english: ℟. His wonders among all peoples.

blocks.source: Oremus, Deus, qui servum tuum S. Ignatium de mundi caesis ad spiritualis militiae triumphos evocasti; praesta quaesumus: ut eum sequamur lucem morum, et protectorem consequamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
blocks.english: Let us pray. O God, who didst call Thy servant Saint Ignatius from [the printed “mundi caesis” is unresolved] to the triumphs of spiritual warfare, grant, we beseech Thee, that we may follow him as a light of conduct, and obtain him as a protector. Through Christ our Lord.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “mundi caesis” is unresolved. No reference to a battlefield or secular life is silently supplied.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Judicio posui te, ut ostenderem te fortitudinem meam, et narretur nomen meum in omni terra.
blocks.english: In judgment I have set thee, that I might show thee My strength, and that My name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth.
blocks.editorialNote: “ostenderem te fortitudinem meam” has defective syntax; the English is provisional without replacing the printed sentence.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis, Sancte Pater Ignati.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, holy Father Ignatius.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus, Deus, qui glorificantes te, glorificas, et in Sanctorum tuorum honoribus honoraris; concede propitius: ut, qui sancti tui Ignatii gloriosa merita colimus ejus apud te pia patrocinia sentiamus. Per Christum Dominum nostrum.
blocks.english: Let us pray. O God, who dost glorify those who glorify Thee, and art honoured in the honours paid to Thy saints, graciously grant that we who venerate the glorious merits of Thy Saint Ignatius may experience his loving patronage before Thee. Through Christ our Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All four printed pages were visually compared. The seven printed hours and all commendation prayers remain; Lauds is not added. The repeated collect incipits expand Matins’ own “Let us pray” and collect, including its printed shortened conclusion. The title’s “Igantius” and defective hymn and prayer clauses remain as printed. Unreadable clauses are explicitly marked unresolved in English, and conjectural readings retain source notes. Hymn line divisions are represented in the prepared English. Vespers has only its printed versicle; no response is invented.
